overall: The committee violated the Open Meeting Law on periodic minute review, late review after a request, insufficient minutes, and an improper executive session vote; two allegations were declined as untimely or unspecific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to timely approve executive session minutes in 2020 and 2021.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the complaint is untimely with respect to any minutes approved more than 30 days prior to the complaint being filed with the Committee, which appears to be all of the minutes at issue in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to periodically review executive session minutes to determine whether they must be released.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acknowledges that it failed to periodically review its executive session minutes to determine whether they needed to be released to the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee did not timely review executive session minutes for release after an April 8 public request.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acknowledges that it did not review the requested executive session minutes at its next meeting following the April 8 request to determine if they must be released, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee continues to improperly withhold unspecified executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: does not identify any particular executive session minutes, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged released executive session minutes were insufficiently detailed and omitted lists of documents used.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes reviewed are insufficient where they do not summarize the discussions that occurred, do not list any documents used during the meetings, and do not record roll call votes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee voted on a transportation agreement in executive session, which was not a permitted purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Where the agreement discussed pertained to services provided by a private company, and not to a collective bargaining agreement, discussion of such agreement was not appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: The request for further review raised additional allegations not included in the formal complaint filed with the committee.
allegations.key_passage: The request for further review raises additional allegations which we decline to review as they were not raised in a formal Open Meeting Law complaint filed with the Committee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Within 60 days, amend the listed executive session minutes to add a summary of all discussions, a list of documents used, and a record of roll call votes, and certify compliance in writing
remedy_passage: We order the Committee, within 60 days of the date of this letter, to amend the minutes for the executive session meetings listed above to include a summary of all discussions held, a list of all documents used, if any, and a record of all roll call votes.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
